definitions.explanation: A mallet with a wooden head, used where a metal hammer would damage the surface—driving chisels, tapping joints together, or striking soft materials. Composed of {木|き} (wood) and {槌|つち} (mallet).

examples.english: Tap it with a wooden mallet.

examples.japanese: {木槌|きづち}で{釘|くぎ}を{軽|かる}く{打|う}った。
examples.english: I lightly drove the nail with a wooden mallet.

examples.japanese: {家具|かぐ}を{組|く}み{立|た}てるとき、{木槌|きづち}を{使|つか}うと{部品|ぶひん}を{傷|きず}つけずに{済|す}む。
examples.english: When assembling furniture, using a wooden mallet lets you avoid damaging the parts.

notes:
Chosen over a metal hammer when the workpiece must not be marked or dented.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {木槌|きづち}で{叩|たた}く: to tap with a wooden mallet
- {木槌|きづち}を{使|つか}う: to use a wooden mallet
- {木槌|きづち}で{打|う}ち{込|こ}む: to drive in with a wooden mallet

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {金槌|かなづち}: metal hammer — harder-hitting but liable to damage soft materials
- ゴムハンマー: rubber mallet — a modern equivalent that leaves no marks
